beats.spoken: Mineral sunscreen never contains nano. That's not quite right.

What counts as nano? Under the EU regulation, it's an insoluble or biopersistent, intentionally manufactured material with one or more external dimensions, or an internal structure, between 1 and 100 nanometres.

In the EU, UV filters can only be used if they're authorised, including as nanomaterials. According to the European Commission, four UV filters have been authorised as nano so far, including titanium dioxide and zinc oxide. Carbon black is also authorised as a nano colourant.
Whether your product contains nano is shown in the ingredient list. Nanomaterials are listed with the word nano in brackets after the name.
And that authorisation isn't automatic. Before colourants, preservatives and UV filters are authorised, including nano forms, the scientific committee SCCS reviews the data submitted.
For you, that means: mineral tells you nothing about particle size. If that matters to you, look for nano in brackets in the ingredient list.
Read the list first, then apply. Beauty knowledge, clearly explained: follow Dewlane.
